precepts.text: The Most High commanded that this month be the beginning of months, and that on the fourteenth day the whole congregation kill the lamb without blemish in the evening.
precepts.point: He commands them to prepare themselves by their courses and stand in the holy place, then kill the Passover, sanctify themselves, and prepare their brethren to do according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
precepts.why:
The Lord spake to Moses and Aaron in Egypt: “This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.” Every man was to take a lamb “according to the house of their fathers”, “without blemish, a male of the first year”, and keep it “until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it in the evening.”

Josiah kept it exactly. “Josiah kept a passover unto the Lord in Jerusalem: and they killed the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.” He kept the laws pertaining to the Passover, in the month the Most High made the beginning of months.

He set it in order: he “set the priests in their charges, and encouraged them to the service of the house of the Lord”, told the Levites to “Put the holy ark in the house which Solomon the son of David king of Israel did build”, and to “prepare yourselves by the houses of your fathers, after your courses”, so the whole congregation could do “according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.”

precepts.text: This day is to be a memorial kept as a feast to the Lord throughout all generations, an ordinance for ever.
precepts.point: He commands them to prepare themselves by their courses and stand in the holy place, then kill the Passover, sanctify themselves, and prepare their brethren to do according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
precepts.why:
“And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to the Lord throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.”

The Passover is a memorial kept as a feast to the Lord throughout all generations, an ordinance for ever. That is why Josiah kept it, and why he charged the Levites, “serve now the Lord your God, and his people Israel”, and to “kill the passover”, “that they may do according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.”

precepts.text: You sanctify yourselves and are holy by keeping the word of the Lord, here the dietary laws, for he is the Lord your God and he is holy.
precepts.point: He commands them to prepare themselves by their courses and stand in the holy place, then kill the Passover, sanctify themselves, and prepare their brethren to do according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
precepts.why:
“For I am the Lord your God: ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.”

You sanctify yourselves and are holy by keeping the word of the Lord, here the dietary laws, for he is the Lord your God and he is holy. That is what Josiah commanded the Levites: “So kill the passover, and sanctify yourselves, and prepare your brethren, that they may do according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.” Sanctifying yourself is doing what the word says.

points: Josiah keeps a Passover unto the Lord in Jerusalem, and they kill the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, keeping the laws pertaining to the Passover.

He sets the priests in their charges, encourages them to the service of the house of the Lord, and tells the Levites to put the holy ark in the house Solomon built and to serve the Lord and his people Israel.

He commands them to prepare themselves by their courses and stand in the holy place, then kill the Passover, sanctify themselves, and prepare their brethren to do according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
Josiah gives the people thirty thousand lambs and kids and three thousand bullocks for the Passover offerings, and his princes give willingly to the people, the priests, and the Levites.

The service is prepared, the priests stand in their place and the Levites in their courses, they kill the Passover, sprinkle the blood, flay the offerings, and roast the Passover with fire according to the ordinance.
The singers, the sons of Asaph, are in their place according to the commandment of David, and the porters wait at every gate so they need not depart from their service.
All the service of the Lord is prepared the same day to keep the Passover and offer burnt offerings on the altar according to the commandment of king Josiah.

The children of Israel present keep the Passover and the feast of unleavened bread seven days, and there was no Passover like it kept in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet; none of the kings of Israel kept such a Passover as Josiah kept in his eighteenth year.

After this, Necho king of Egypt comes up to fight at Carchemish by Euphrates, and Josiah goes out against him though Necho sends word that his war is not with Josiah and that God had commanded him to make haste.
Josiah will not turn his face but disguises himself to fight, hearkening not to the words of Necho from the mouth of God, and the archers shoot him in the valley of Megiddo.

His servants take him from the chariot and bring him to Jerusalem, where he dies and is buried, and all Judah and Jerusalem mourn, and Jeremiah laments for Josiah, written in the Lamentations, a book of the Bible.
The rest of the acts of Josiah and his goodness, according to that which is written in the law of the Lord, and his deeds first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
